meta.text: Let's reason through a worked example: an 8 GB build side joined against a 3 GB probe side. The build side is 8 GB — that's way above the autoBroadcastJoinThreshold, so BHJ is off. Neither side is small enough to be a clean broadcast candidate, and 3 GB shuffled against 8 GB is a large-to-large join. Spark will fall back to Sort-Merge Join here, shuffling and sorting both sides. That matches our trigger-condition rule: broadcast needs a genuinely small side.
